thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2965432100 - Suspicious auth token reuse detected across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Service: inference-auth-proxy. Severity: P1. Paging oncall-alex.

oncall-alex: Ack, I'm on it. Can you post the affected endpoints and sample request IDs?

pagerbot: Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (us-east-1), /v1/auth/validate (eu-west-1). Sample request_ids: rq_8f3a, rq_b71c, rq_2d9e. 401 spike started ~2026-03-17T09:32:17Z.

sara: seeing elevated 401s and some internal retries. cpu on auth-proxy pods spiked ~3x on us-east-1, connections at 95% of limit. Noticable tail latency increase.

infra-bot: pulling logs from staging-forwarder: 
```
2026-03-17T09:31:58Z inference-auth-proxy request_id=rq_8f3a auth_token=tok_XXXX status=401 src=10.10.45.72
2026-03-17T09:32:03Z log-forwarder svc=staging-s3 forward=PUT bucket=redwood-staging-logs key=logs/2026-03-17/auth/rq_8f3a.json
```

matt: suspicious pattern: same auth token used from two different regions within 30s. Possible token leak or replay. Any recent deploys touching forwarder or auth token handling?

sara: small deploy to log-forwarder 09:20Z this morning that enabled region fanout for dev/staging logs. I can roll that back if needed.

security-lead: Do NOT roll anything that will delete logs. Legal preserves. We need to contain, rotate compromised tokens, and identify customer impact. Matt, can you confirm whether tokens in those logs are production tokens or staging?

matt: The token prefix matches prod shape. Cross-checked against active session index: tok_9a.. appears in 4 active sessions. Recommend immediate rotation of the service token used by auth-proxy and a short-lived blocklist for the observed tokens.

oncall-alex: Executing rotation now. Running key rotation script on auth-proxy service. Will switch traffic to secondary key after validation.

oncall-alex: ```bash
./ops/rotate-service-key --service=inference-auth-proxy --rotate-active=true --dry-run=false
```

infra-bot: Rotation job started (job_id=rot_20260317_01). Noting dependent services: api-gateway, dedicated-router, metrics-consumer. Will propagate in ~30s.

pagerbot: Customer impact flags: some customers will see auth errors if they have long-lived tokens tied to the old service key. Initial estimate: ~0.6% of requests in the last hour, concentrated in a small set of high-traffic tenants.

matt: I'm running a quick query to map affected customer IDs. Holding on communication until we have scope. Suggest setting rate-limit fallback and enabling secondary auth provider for critical tenants.

sara: Canary rollback of the log-forwarder deploy queued (not executed) until we know rotation outcome. If rotation fails, we'll revert.

legal: Preserve all logs/objects under redwood-staging-logs and redwood-prod-logs. Do not purge or redact until we confirm. Create a snapshot and provide path to security.

security-lead: After rotation completes, we will 1) revoke exposed tokens, 2) add temporary WAF rule to block anomalous src IPs, 3) audit S3 access logs for exfil traces, 4) prepare customer comms. Handing over to security on-call (matt) for deep triage. oncall-alex, keep monitoring and escalate to infra if propagation issues appear.

oncall-alex: Rotation succeeded, job_id=rot_20260317_01, primary key switched. Monitoring auth success rate.

infra-bot: Auth success rate recovered to baseline in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. No immediate downstream errors observed.

matt: Beginning forensic pull: correlating tokens, IPs, and S3 access. Will update in #incidents-security with findings. Assigning P1 security ticket SEC-2026-112.

security-lead: Thanks team — handoff complete. oncall-alex, please add timeline to the ticket and include commands executed. Closing pager until new alerts. :lock:

oncall-alex: Added timeline and command outputs to SEC-2026-112. Marking as monitoring.

pagerbot: INCIDENT 2965432100 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Close if no regression in 2h.
